changelog.cited_in_range_count._rationale: 2026-08-15 fleet spawn census re-verification (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-census-reverification-at-head.md § 'Rows surviving intact and unguarded'): `_cited_in_range_count` spawned one `git rev-parse --verify` per unique hex-looking token found via regex over a free-text changelog body -- unbounded by construction, no memo, no timeout. Fix: `_batch_resolve_commits` resolves the whole token set in ONE `git cat-file --batch-check` process (stdin-fed, `timeout=_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT`), each token queried as `{tok}^{commit}` to match the prior per-token `rev-parse --verify -q {tok}^{commit}` peel byte-for-byte -- the set of tokens classified as resolving to a commit is unchanged, only the spawn shape is. `target_ms`/`tolerance` satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape only; `spawn_count_budget` is the enforced invariant, guarded by `coordinator_core/ops/test_changelog_cited_in_range_spawn_bound.py`. `n_tokens=1`: any nonzero number of distinct tokens costs exactly one subprocess (was N before the fix). `no_tokens=0`: an empty token set short-circuits before spawning at all.

percolate.functional_identifier_output_d._rationale: 2026-08-15 audit (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-census-reverification-at-head.md row 7): `find_functional_identifier_output_drift_in_tree` (coordinator_core/percolate/store.py) ran `_git_commit_epoch_time` -- one `git log -1 --format=%ct` spawn -- per candidate file whenever a caller supplied `dest_publish_time`, unbounded by construction. This op's sole non-test caller, `publish.py`'s `dispatch_end_of_run_functional_identifier_output_drift_check`, never supplies `dest_publish_time` (its own docstring: 'that branch forks one git log per file ... and is what killed two prior measurement attempts on this machine's shared, heavily-loaded tree'), so the branch is currently reachable only from tests -- `no_dest_publish_time=0` documents the production caller's actual (unchanged, already-zero) spawn count. Fix: `_git_commit_epoch_times_batch` resolves the whole candidate-file set in ONE `git log --format=%x00%ct --name-only -- <paths...>` spawn (newest-commit-first, first occurrence per path wins, matching `git log -1 --format=%ct -- path` semantics exactly) instead of one spawn per file, for any FUTURE caller that does supply `dest_publish_time` -- the set of drift triples returned is unchanged, only the spawn shape is. `target_ms`/`tolerance` satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape only; `spawn_count_budget` is the enforced invariant, guarded by `coordinator_core/percolate/tests/test_functional_identifier_output_drift_spawn_budget.py`. `with_dest_publish_time_n_files=1`: any nonzero number of candidate files costs exactly one subprocess (was N before the fix) once `dest_publish_time` is supplied.

bin.coordinator_harvest_deferrals_dedup_._rationale: 2026-08-15 audit (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-composed-op-spawn-census.md row 13 / state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-census-reverification-at-head.md): `coordinator-harvest-deferrals.py::_harvest`'s per-row loop calls `_candidate_search_dirs(row)` for every candidate, which in turn calls `_repo_root()` (a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocess spawn), `_resolved_doe_root()`, and `_resolved_claude_klabauter_root()` (each capable of its own machine-local-registry/marketplace-cache subprocess spawn) FRESH per row -- 3 resolution calls x N rows for an answer invariant for the whole process's lifetime. The per-row WRITE dispatch itself (`_run_queue_append`/`_run_lesson_promote`, already timeout-bounded at `_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_SECS`, and since the 2026-08-15 staff review also catches `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and degrades it to a per-row failure) is deliberately left one-spawn-per-row -- each row's write stays isolated via the `_run_*` helpers' return-False contract, not a `try` inside `_harvest()` itself, so one row's failure or hang never blocks another's. Fix (root resolution): memoize the three resolution calls (`_repo_root_cache`/`_resolved_doe_root_cache`/`_resolved_claude_klabauter_root_cache`, first-call-wins, mirroring the pre-existing `_CLI_CMD_CACHE` pattern). Fix (directory scan, 2026-08-15 staff review Defect 2 -- the expensive half of the per-row work an earlier pass left unhoisted): `_already_harvested` re-globbed AND re-read EVERY `*.yaml` file in up to four directories (`state/improvement-queue`, `state/lessons-outbox`, in both claude-klabauter and DoE) ONCE PER CANDIDATE ROW -- `_derive_proposed_action`'s own docstring measures those corpora at 605/493 entries, i.e. O(rows x ~1100 full file reads) for a key set invariant across the loop. `_collect_evidence_lines(search_dirs)` now does that glob+read ONCE, before the loop, returning the flat list of `evidence:`-prefixed lines; `_already_harvested(key, evidence_lines)` is then an O(1)-per-row substring membership check against that pre-collected list, preserving the exact prior match semantics (line must start with `evidence:`, key checked via substring). `target_ms`/`tolerance` are carried only to satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape -- this key is not a real op, `spawn_count_budget` is the enforced invariant. Enforced by `coordinator/bin/tests/test_harvest_deferrals_dedup_scan_memoized.py` (`resolution_calls_for_5_candidate_rows=1` -- exactly one SPAWN from `_resolved_claude_klabauter_root()` regardless of candidate-row count, fixture: 5 rows, versus 15 pre-fix; lowered from 3 to 2 on 2026-08-17 because eacbba04a routed `_repo_root()` through `coordinator_core.git.repo_root.show_toplevel`, which walks for the ordinary case and spawns only when the walk finds no `.git` entry -- the budget counts spawns, so that third call is no longer one; lowered again from 2 to 1 (2026-08-26) because `coordinator_registry.doe_root()`'s rung 2 (`repos.doe_claude`) is now an in-process read via `machine_local_impl_resolve.registry_get()`, CLI spawn retained only as a fallback rung -- `_resolved_doe_root()` no longer spawns in the steady state where that in-process read resolves. Memoization of all three is unchanged and still asserted; do NOT raise this back to make a regression pass) and `coordinator/bin/tests/test_harvest_deferrals_evidence_scan_hoisted.py` (`directory_scan_calls_for_5_candidate_rows=1` -- `_collect_evidence_lines`/the underlying `glob.glob`+file-read pass runs exactly once per `_harvest()` invocation regardless of candidate-row count, versus once per row pre-fix; asserts the CALL COUNT of the scan, not wall-clock).

bin.workday_complete_close_backfill_disp._rationale: 2026-08-15 audit (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-composed-op-spawn-census.md row 14): `workday-complete-close.py::cmd_backfill_dispatch_rows` dispatches ONE full composed step9-ceremony subprocess (`_dispatch_step9_row`) per gap date, up to the 14-day lookback -- deliberately left one-spawn-per-gap-date: each row's exit code is tracked independently and the loop's own contract ('one bad day should not abandon the rest of the backfill') requires row N's failure to never block row N+1's dispatch, so batching into a single invocation is NOT equivalent and was rejected. `_dispatch_step9_row`'s previously-unbounded `subprocess.run` now carries `timeout=_STEP9_ROW_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECS` (120s), with a `TimeoutExpired` caught and converted to a per-row failure (rc=1) rather than crashing the whole loop, preserving per-row isolation under a timeout the same as under a subprocess failure. `target_ms`/`tolerance` are carried only to satisfy `budget.py._validated_budget`'s required override shape -- this key is not a real op. 2026-08-15 staff review: a prior `spawn_count_budget.spawns_per_gap_date=1` was removed here -- it was N==N (true by definition for any one-spawn-per-row implementation, bounds nothing) and its docstring wording actively forbade the correct duplicate-date dedup fix (workday-complete-close.py::cmd_backfill_dispatch_rows now skips a re-seen date rather than re-dispatching it), which would have made a 3-row input with one duplicate cost 2 spawns and broken that tautological assertion. The real invariants (timeout present on every row dispatch; a duplicated date dispatches once, not twice; one row's timeout does not abort the rest) are behavioural, not spawn-count-shaped, and are enforced directly by `coordinator/bin/tests/test_workday_complete_backfill_dispatch_timeout.py` without a manifest budget.

C3 recorded 37 the same day from a standalone repro script (not shipped); the plan's origin figure was also '~37 per close'. ATTRIBUTION OF THE -3 IS OPEN and must not be restated as settled: it is a REDUCTION, so banking it only makes the ratchet stricter, and an unbanked reduction is itself a ratchet failure. Leading candidate is a1e5dd970 (15:36, wsc-tail review-trail records folded into the ceremony commit's pathspec), which touched wsc_tail.py after C3 measured; the alternative is a harness difference between C3's script and this fixture. Neither established. C4 (docs/plans/2026-08-21-the-census-that-cannot-miss-an-op.md), migrated from a test-local pin (test_wsc_tail_spawn_budget.py's own `_WSC_TAIL_OP_TOTAL_CEILING`, deleted in the same change) into this manifest, ratcheted by test_spawn_count_budget_ratchet.py's same exact-equality `spawn_count_budget` convention (the `ceremony.scoped_git_commit` row this comparison used to point at was itself dropped at 5fff9d4e8, per K-045's residual-bookkeeping cleanup). ops.discover_working_repos._spawn_count_rationale: Two LAYERS of key, deliberately. The op_total_* keys are the OP: main() end-to-end, nothing stubbed, measured 2026-08-19 (opro-03 C6) at 3 / 3 / 0 for the Tier-A-non-empty, Tier-B-fallback and all-tiers-empty shapes. Three because _sort_unique shells to sort -u once per NON-EMPTY call and main() reaches it three times -- _tier_a's tail, _tier_a5's tail, and main's own merge tail; the all-empty shape is 0 because _sort_unique early-returns on an empty list without spawning. That shell-out is a SANCTIONED carve-out (test_no_bash_dependency.py names it, for byte-parity with the bash oracle), so it is counted, not removed; reducing it is a carve-out decision, not a budget one. The other two keys are SUB-PATHS and must not be read as the op total: per_call=1 is _tier_a5 alone, and machine_local_cli_elimination_calls=0 isolates _merged_flat_registry's elimination of the per-key machine-local CLI spawns, legitimately stubbing _sort_unique to do so. History worth keeping: per_call was 0 until 2026-08-19 because the asserting test monkeypatched out _sort_unique -- the one function on that path that spawns -- immediately before counting, so the figure was true of a stubbed op and false of this one. The op total went unmeasured for longer still because _tier_a reads Path.home()/.claude/projects and the pre-existing COORDINATOR_TIER_A_FS_ROOT seam covers only the existence probe; COORDINATOR_TIER_A_PROJECTS_DIR was added to make a hermetic main() count possible at all. No spawn was ever added by any of this -- each raise made an existing spawn countable. Trace: state/audits/2026-08-19-opro-03-c08-budgeted-op-spawn-trace.md.
ops.discover_working_repos._rationale: 2026-08-15 staff review of the fleet spawn sweep (state/audits/2026-08-15-fleet-census-reverification-at-head.md). discover_working_repos.py::_tier_a5 spawned one machine-local keys subprocess plus one machine-local get <key> per repos.* key, and ::_publish_mirror_keys independently repeated the whole pattern for publish.mirrors.*.path -- measured live at ~24 interpreter spawns per main() call (19 repos keys + 4 mirror paths), each with a 10s timeout, on a box CLAUDE.md sizes at 50-70 concurrent LLM sessions. This was not merely slow: it contradicted the standing negative spec in coordinator_core/machine_resolver.py, which forbids shelling out to that CLI, and the 2026-08-05 PM directive on de-bashing spawn amplification that it records. It was also LESS CORRECT than a direct read -- registry_get's docstring notes the CLI lives under a resettable bin directory, so the CLI working is not proof of reset-survival, while a direct file read is. Fix: _merged_flat_registry merges registry.local.toml over registry.toml via machine_resolver.load_flat_registry_file/registry_dir (direct tomllib), zero subprocesses. Concern-layer parity was verified rather than assumed: _machine_local.py::_flatten_nested documents these keys as root-namespace-only and actively drops concern-name collisions, so a flat two-file read cannot miss a repo. target_ms/tolerance satisfy budget.py._validated_budget's required override shape only; spawn_count_budget is the enforced invariant, guarded by coordinator_core/ops/test_discover_working_repos_spawn_budget.py. per_call=0 is a real ceiling, not a per-item ratio -- any key count costs zero subprocesses, so a regression to the CLI fails at 1.

reverification.why: The 2026-08-23 rows entered the repo through a human safety sweep (8350b8fa0), never through their own session's commit, and no gate ran against them. Re-measured before anything was built on them.
reverification.method: coordinator_core.benchmarks.process_time.batched_process_time_ms, k=20, five independent repeats per arm, 2026-08-25 on the same box.
reverification.verdict: The 2026-08-23 figures (38.281 / 47.656) DO NOT REPRODUCE. Five repeats of each arm sit ~1.5x below them and outside their spread. The direction survives -- the transport removes one whole child process -- but the magnitude is ~27-32ms of child process time per hook fire, not ~47.7ms, and the engine-import increment over a bare interpreter is ~4-5ms, not ~9.4ms.
reverification.retracted_claim: "That figure is stable" is withdrawn. Both arms sit within two Windows scheduler ticks (~15.6ms) of each other, so a single k=20 batch cannot separate them; only the repeat spread can, and the spread is what moved.

c4_supervised_listener.method: Listener bound IN-PROCESS around the production supervisor._make_handler; arms interleaved round-robin, n=30, 3 warmup rounds discarded. Every primitive measured is the real one.
c4_supervised_listener.not_exercised: ensure_listener's spawn_detached leg. Spawning a resident process on a box running 50-70 sessions to take a number is the litter class the is_engine_root gate exists to prevent. Boot latency is therefore NOT in any figure below.
c4_supervised_listener.reads_the_p90_correctly: min and p50 sit under 0.7ms on all three arms; p90 jumps to ~14-15ms on the two that touch a socket. That is PEER LOAD, not transport cost -- the same 0.6 -> 14.4ms movement the 2026-08-23 rows recorded across runs with identical code, now reproduced within a single interleaved run. Quote min alongside any p50; never quote a p90 from this box as an arm cost.

p_listener_up.shape: coordinator_core.benchmarks.listener_availability (8f49c9cc7) --sample --engine-root X:/claude-klabauter --interval 60. read_discovery + GET /health only: never ensure_listener (which would measure its own side effect), never the C door (which falls through to cold Python and so cannot report down), never POST /hook.
p_listener_up.ownership_correction: The prior note called sampling the stamped clone 'a cross-repo action with its own owner'. That inverted the ownership: X:/claude-klabauter is claude-klabauter's own publish mirror. No cross-repo ask was needed and none was made.
p_listener_up.what_this_does_not_support: A steady-state claim across a working day, or time-of-day variation. DoE's own pipe-server sampling on this box found a 31.5-minute outage caused by a percolate deleting the build stamp (docs/research/2026-08-25-http-listener-availability.md) -- a routine, repeatable deploy event this window did not span. The risk on this transport is deploys, not churn, and this number does not measure deploys.
p_listener_up.reading: 1.0 is the observed rate over 36 samples with zero recorded failures -- not an established availability. Rule-of-three (3/n, n=36) puts the one-sided 95% upper bound on the failure rate at ~8.3% (failure_rate_upper_95 above); a risk calculation should use that bound, not the point estimate.
p_listener_up.what_was_probed: GET /health reachability of the listener process/socket only, via supervisor.check_health. This establishes listener process/socket availability, not /hook-dispatch functional health -- a wedge isolated to POST /hook dispatch (an exception in hook_http.build_request/_serve_line, a ctx.dispatch deadlock, GIL contention on the POST path) is invisible to this probe and would still read up. Not probed via POST /hook by design: that would put synthetic guard traffic on a resident server serving dozens of sessions.
p_listener_up.why_it_is_no_longer_the_blocker: 1.0 over this window. What actually blocked the twenty non-deny-capable registrations was claude-klabauter-side and is fixed in 399a72b4b: the transport framed every event with GUARD_OP_NAME, forwarded only the guard's fields, and dropped additionalContext/systemMessage on every success.
p_listener_up.recount_note: n corrected 36 -> 50 before commit. The sampler kept appending after the first read, so the recorded n no longer reproduced from the JSONL it cites -- a figure that disagrees with its own source is the defect, whichever number is larger. Recomputed from state/measurements/http-listener-availability.jsonl in full.

per_term_attribution.headline: real-relay process p90 218.8 -> 156.25 ms, a 62.55ms reduction.
per_term_attribution.term_1_relay_floor: The control arm -- identical relay, two stubbed no-ops, zero op work -- moved from 140.6ms p90 to 93.75ms p90. This is the relay machinery itself, and it accounts for 46.85ms of the 62.55ms.
per_term_attribution.term_2_the_two_ops_own_cost: Real minus control: 78.2ms p90 before (218.8-140.6), 62.5ms now (156.25-93.75). The two catering ops add 15.7ms less than they did.
per_term_attribution.why_this_is_not_a_residual: Both terms are measured arms, not one arm and a subtraction. The control is a real run of the same relay with the op bodies stubbed, so the floor is observed rather than inferred -- which is what this plan Anti-scope demands ("Do not attribute a cost by subtraction ... a residual is not an attribution"). The subtraction that remains, real minus control, is the difference of TWO measured quantities rather than an unexplained remainder.

_ac8_subagent_start_relay_remeasure.spawn_count_note: SETTLED 2026-08-25 (pickup), replacing the open question this key previously recorded. THE RELAY GENUINELY SPAWNS NOTHING; the enumeration is not blind. Direct measurement, invocation shape stated: batched_process_time_ms([sys.executable, '-c', <script>], k=3, cwd=_REPO_ROOT) reads procs_per_call 1.0 for the real relay arm, 1.0 for the control arm, 1.0 for a bare `pass` script (the root-inclusive floor, which fixes the convention), and 2.0 for a script that deliberately spawns one child -- same primitive, same k, same cwd. An instrument that reads 2.0 on a deliberate child in the identical call is observing the relay's zero, not missing its spawns. enumerate_spawn_set's independent Popen-patch view agrees at [], and the two disagree in what they could miss (the job object is spawn-mechanism-blind and catches os.system/posix_spawn; the Popen patch catches only in-process Popen constructions), so their agreement is corroboration rather than one instrument counted twice. A DEFECT FOUND SETTLING IT, now fixed: spawn_count = max(0, round(procs_per_call) - 1) is NOT injective at the low end -- procs_per_call 0.0 and 1.0 both derive to spawn_count 0. 0.0 is a reading the primitive really produces (see _hook_seam_http_transport's warm arms), so the collapse is reachable rather than theoretical, and the recorded 0.0 in this block structurally COULD NOT have answered its own question. catering_path_bench now records raw procs_per_call alongside spawn_count for exactly this reason. The p50/p90/max 0.0 figures in real_relay/control_relay above predate that and are read here against the direct measurement, not on their own.
_ac8_subagent_start_relay_remeasure.instrument_fix_required_to_take_this_mea: catering_path_bench refused to run on Windows at all until 2026-08-25. Its `_verify_spawn_count_derivation` known-truth fixture was `python -> git --version`, DERIVED at 2.0 root-inclusive; measured here it reads 3.0 deterministically (5/5) against a 1.0 no-child baseline, because Git for Windows spawns a helper of its own. The derivation under test was never wrong -- its oracle binary was. Swapped to `python -> python -c pass`, whose child count is a property of CPython rather than of whichever git build is on PATH. The guard fired correctly on a fixture that could not hold.

spawn_count_raw_procs_per_call.reading: root-inclusive. 1.0 = the interpreter itself and zero children.
spawn_count_raw_procs_per_call.why_a_positive_control: A zero from an instrument nobody proved is looking is not a measurement. The 2.0 arm is what makes the three 1.0s evidence.
